dedupe_keys.name: explaining building damage from wildfires in california 100 m damage risk layer and analysis ready dins dataset

description: This Dryad dataset supports a study that models and explains wildfire damage to buildings in California's wildland-urban interface, by Somnath Bar, Shu Li and Tirtha Banerjee, published on 23 June 2026 and cited by a Science Advances article. The authors used over 100,000 CAL FIRE damage inspection (DINS) records from 2013 to 2024 with topography, vegetation, human footprint, daily weather and a Composite Building Flammability Rating to train Random Forest classifiers: the full model reached 88% accuracy, 82.9% without the flammability rating and 74.5% with environmental exposure alone, and building flammability, dew point and near-surface wind were the strongest predictors. Causal forests estimate spatially varying treatment effects. Files are a 100 m GeoTIFF of wildfire building damage probability for California from the environmental exposure model, an analysis-ready CSV derived from LANDFIRE, NLCD, DINS, DAYMET and building footprints, and R, Python and notebook code for the whole workflow. Coverage: California, calibrated on fires from 2013 to 2024. Access: about 387 MB on Dryad, DOI 10.5061/dryad.r2280gbrw. Licence: CC0 1.0; free. Caveats: the raster excludes building attributes, spatial cross-validation accuracy falls to 62-68%, and county boundaries must be fetched separately. Simulation uses are wildfire exposure and building vulnerability layers for risk and mitigation planning. Related records: the California Chapter 7A building code natural experiment and Palisades Fire structure loss records.
name: Explaining building damage from wildfires in California: 100 m damage risk layer and analysis-ready DINS dataset
